dedupe_keys.name: phes odm public health environmental surveillance open data model wastewater surveillance data standard

description: PHES-ODM is an open data model and dictionary for wastewater and environmental surveillance data. It began as a standard for SARS-CoV-2 wastewater surveillance and version 2 extended it to surface and air testing and to any biological, toxin or other health risk; it defines 15 report tables and six look-up tables for sites, sewersheds, samples, measures, methods and organisations, in long or wide format. The project, begun in Canada and run with an international steering committee, publishes the dictionary as CSV files and SQL schemas on GitHub, an Excel dictionary and report templates on OSF, documentation and a validation toolkit, all free to download under CC BY 4.0; datasets such as the Delatolla Lab's Canadian surveillance database on Zenodo are published in the format. Coverage is global in intent, and the README calls it one of the de facto global wastewater surveillance data standards. Caveats: the project entered a long-term maintenance phase in September 2026, so responses to issues may be slower, and it is a structure for data, not data itself. Simulation uses: harmonising sewershed surveillance feeds for outbreak emergency response and public-health digital twins. Related records: the US NWSS (data-cdc-nwss-wastewater-surveillance) and Germany's AMELAG (data-rki-amelag-wastewater-surveillance).
